entries.claim: The regression coverage never exercises the documented multibyte boundary immediately before an ASCII assignment name; every process-boundary test asserts only `café=1` and `Größe=10`, while the changelog separately claims the curly-quoted assignment is fixed.
entries.failure_scenario: Revert or break only the fix for backward scanning when a multibyte opening quote directly precedes an ASCII secret name, such as the changelog's `“<redacted>` case. Scanning names that themselves contain `é` or `ß` can remain safe, so the MCP, brief, prompt, search, and show tests all pass, yet enabling `redact_recall` still panics on the documented curly-quoted secret assignment. The fixture is described as containing that case, but none of the new assertions requires it to be processed or redacted.

counter_evidence.note: The curly-quoted case is pinned directly by the unit test at egress.rs:1392, which asserts for_model_context turns “token=abc” into “token=[redacted], so a partial revert that broke only that case fails there. The process-boundary tests also run the same fixture turn, which holds “token=abc” beside café=1 and Größe=10, and Bench::call fails on any panic on stderr. All three strings broke through the one rfind-plus-one slice the fix replaced; there is no separate fix for the curly case to revert alone.
